data.title: Week ahead: BoE announcement, non-farm payrolls in focus
data.description:
On Monday half-year results from Ryanair are due, while in the US, quarterly results from Apple and Palantir will be eyed. On the macro front, the S&P Global UK manufacturing PMI for October will be among the highlights.

AJ Bell analysts Russ Mould, Danni Hewson and Dan Coatsworth said: "It’s trick or treat time for new CEO John Ternus who has an opportunity to put his stamp on Apple’s AI strategy and future direction.

"Apple’s decision to raise the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max could ease margin pressure from rising component costs, but investors will be watching for signs of consumer pushback.

"With the shares trading close to all-time highs, Apple’s premium valuation means investors will be looking for more than Apple’s customary earnings beat.

"With only nine days of iPhone 18 Pro sales and no iPhone Duo revenue in the quarter, the market reaction is likely to be driven by Christmas guidance. Management may also be expected to address ‘Crackgate’ with reports on social media of problems with the screens on the new Duo model."

On Tuesday, Primark owner Associated British Foods will release full-year results, while TP Icap, Hiscox and IWG will put out third-quarter trading updates. Across the pond, AMD, Shopify and Pfizer are slated to report Q3 results.

Investors will also look out for the latest policy announcement from the Reserve Bank of Australia.

Wednesday will be busy on the UK corporate front, with trading updates from Barratt Redrow, Coca-Cola HBC, JD Wetherspoon, Lancashire Holdings, Prudential and Smith & Nephew, and half-year results from Trainline.

In the US, quarterly results from Arm, Qualcomm, McDonald’s and Uber Technologies will be in focus.

On the macro front, preliminary eurozone inflation figures for October will be out, along with UK and eurozone PMIs for October.

On Thursday, the corporate calendar will be busy again, with half-year results from Auto Trader, BT Group and Tate & Lyle, Q3 results from Helios Towers and a trading and operations update from Harbour Energy. Trading updates from Next, Vistry Group, Croda, Howden Joinery, Morgan Sindall and OSB Group will also be released.

In the US, quarterly earnings from ConocoPhillips and Cloudflare will be in focus.

In the UK, all eyes will be on the latest policy announcement from the Bank of England, which is widely expected to raise interest rates by 25 basis points to 4%. This would mark the first move in the base rate of 2026.

Rabobank expects the MPC to raise Bank Rate to 4% in a 7-2 split vote. "Whether they like it or not, persistent energy inflation is increasingly forcing the MPC’s hand, even as there is limited evidence of broader second-round effects," it said.

"We have raised our 2027 inflation forecast to 3.9%, driven primarily by higher energy price forecasts.

"We therefore add a second 25bp hike in February 2027, taking Bank Rate to 4.25%, with further moves remaining largely dependent on the situation in the Middle East."

On Friday, British Airways and Iberia owner IAG will release third-quarter earnings. On the macro calendar, the US non-farm payrolls report for October will be in the spotlight, along with average earnings and the unemployment rate.

data.title: Is it legal to recruit spoiler candidates in US elections?
data.description:
Key points:
  • Two people named Dan Sullivan appear on Alaska ballot
  • New York Times reported Democrats recruited spoiler candidates
  • Justice Department has sought to potentially block certification

By Luc Cohen and Tom Hals

The Justice Department is investigating allegations that Democrats recruited potential spoiler candidates to run in Alaska’s US Senate race, and has asked a US judge to prevent certification of the vote if incumbent Republican Senator Daniel S. Sullivan loses narrowly.

The race, in which Democratic former US Representative Mary Peltola is challenging Sullivan, could prove critical for determining the balance of power in the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections. President Donald Trump’s fellow Republicans are battling to maintain majorities in both chambers.

Below is an explanation of the legal issues at play and why the Justice Department will face challenges in its civil lawsuit or any criminal case.

WHAT IS THE STATE OF THE ALASKA RACE?

Alaska’s ranked-choice ballot will feature Sullivan, Peltola, a retired teacher whose name is also Daniel Sullivan, and another long-shot candidate.

Earlier this week, the New York Times reported that Peltola’s aides worked with the campaign’s lawyers and senior staff at Senate Democrats’ campaign arm to recruit the retired teacher Daniel J. Sullivan. Reuters has not verified the report.

Trump has called for Peltola to be prosecuted, and Alaska’s Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered a state law enforcement investigation. Neither Trump nor Dunleavy specified which laws they believed may have been violated.

The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee has denied involvement and said Republicans had also propped up other candidates in an attempt to boost their own campaigns.

Daniel J. Sullivan has denied coordinating with Peltola's campaign.

Peltola's campaign did not respond to a request for comment. Its lawyers have asked US District Judge Sharon Gleason to dismiss the Justice Department's lawsuit, arguing the federal government lacks the legal authority to bring the case.

Alaska's ballot will indicate that Daniel S. Sullivan is the incumbent.

COULD THE TIMES REPORT AFFECT THE OUTCOME OF THE DOJ LAWSUIT?

The Justice Department's case seeking to prevent certification of election results if the incumbent Daniel S. Sullivan loses by a slim margin is pending.

Alaska’s elections regulator earlier this year blocked Daniel J. Sullivan from appearing on the ballot, finding that his candidacy was not filed in good faith and was instead an attempt to “confuse or mislead.”

State courts later restored him to the ballot, ruling that there was not enough evidence that he was trying to confuse voters and that there was no requirement under Alaska law that a candidacy be in good faith.

Legal experts have said the Justice Department's case is weak because the US Constitution clearly assigns the responsibility for administering elections to the states, not the federal government.

Joshua Douglas, a law professor at the University of Kentucky, said the reporting asserting that Democrats helped recruit spoiler candidates was unlikely to help the Justice Department's case.

"Regardless of who encouraged him to run, the second Dan Sullivan validly qualified for the ballot. And this is a matter of state law," Douglas said.

Gleason's decision on Peltola's motion to dismiss the Justice Department's lawsuit could come as soon as Saturday, though it is not certain when she will rule.

WHAT CRIMINAL LAWS COULD BE AT PLAY?

Legal experts said the Justice Department could seek to bring a criminal case under a federal statute that makes it illegal for any two people to conspire to deprive anyone of their constitutional rights, including the right to vote.

The law, originally passed in 1871 to combat the Ku Klux Klan, makes it illegal to conspire to “injure, oppress, threaten, or intimidate any person” to prevent them from exercising a right.

In addition, if anyone lied under oath in earlier state-level litigation over whether Dan J. Sullivan could appear on the ballot, they could be prosecuted for perjury, UCLA law professor Rick Hasen wrote in an October 28 blog post.

WOULD ANY PROSECUTION BE VIABLE?

Hasen said any federal criminal prosecution under the conspiracy-against-rights would likely fail because the free speech guarantees in the First Amendment to the US Constitution would likely protect the right to run for office with “impure motives.”

Michael Fragoso, a former lawyer for Republican Senator Mitch McConnell, said “dirty tricks” — such as one major party trying to help a fringe candidate win over voters from the other major party — were generally legal. But he said convincing voters they were voting for their preferred candidate when they were not was different.

“It’s suppressing disfavored votes by tricking voters into thinking that they’re voting one way when in fact, they aren’t,” Fragoso, now a fellow at the Washington-based think tank Ethics and Public Policy Center, wrote in an October 28 blog post in the National Review.

IS THERE ANY LEGAL PRECEDENT?

In a case brought by the Justice Department under Democratic President Joe Biden’s administration, a social media influencer was convicted in 2023 in Brooklyn federal court of conspiring against civil rights by using social media posts to spread false information about the 2016 election to help Trump win.

The Manhattan-based 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals in 2025 overturned that conviction, finding a lack of evidence he conspired with anyone. The appeals court’s decision did not address the influencer's argument that the First Amendment would protect speech deceiving voters.

data.title: Terex Reports Third-Quarter Sales Growth, Raises Free Cash Flow Outlook
data.description:
Terex reported third-quarter sales of $2.2 billion, up 11.6% on a pro forma basis, and adjusted EBITDA of $286 million. Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.50, while operating cash flow reached $241 million. The company updated its 2026 outlook, including a free cash flow range of $360 million to $400 million.

Financial Highlights

  • Third-quarter sales were $2.2 billion, up $229 million, or 11.6%, on a pro forma basis.
  • Adjusted EBITDA increased $35 million to $286 million; adjusted EBITDA margin was 13.0%.
  • Adjusted diluted EPS was $1.50. The release did not state gross profit, operating income or net income.
  • Operating cash flow was $241 million and free cash flow was $209 million. Terex returned $91 million to shareholders and paid down $113 million of debt.
  • For 2026, Terex expects sales of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion, adjusted pro forma EBITDA of $930 million to $960 million, EPS of $4.80 to $5.00, and free cash flow of $360 million to $400 million.

Business Highlights

  • Third-quarter bookings rose 53% year over year on a pro forma basis, with growth in all four segments. Backlog reached $7 billion, and consolidated book-to-bill was approximately 103%.
  • Materials Processing bookings and backlog strengthened, with backlog reaching a two-year high. Specialty Vehicles reported growth in bookings across end markets and is expanding capacity at its Brandon facility to reduce lead times.
  • Environmental Solutions bookings improved, led by refuse collection vehicle orders. Terex is expanding Utilities production capacity, while teams work through ramp-up inefficiencies at Waukesha and Birmingham.
  • Aerials bookings increased amid demand from national customers serving large infrastructure projects. Terex advanced the segment’s separation process and is engaging with multiple strategic counterparties.
  • Terex launched a centralized procurement organization and continued integration and operating-improvement work. Product introductions included Heil’s next-generation automated side loader and Finlay’s Elektro hybrid crushing range; the company also exited Capacity and Laymor.

Original SEC Filing: TEREX CORP [ TEX ] - 8-K - Oct. 30, 2026

data.title: Starbucks CEO: "I would never say never to a multi-brand future"
data.description:
Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol said in a Bloomberg Television interview on Friday that the coffee chain could eventually expand beyond its core brand into a multi-brand business.

Asked about the possibility, Niccol called it “one of those possibilities,” adding that Starbucks’ scale provided an opportunity to go beyond being a one-brand company.

He said Starbucks’ immediate priority remained its internal growth strategy, which focused on upgrading stores, improving menus, and enhancing customer service.

However, he did not rule out a broader portfolio in the future, saying that adding other businesses that could leverage Starbucks’ strengths “could be an interesting proposition, down the road.”

He also said the company could meet its growth targets without acquisitions.

A multi-brand approach would resemble Yum! Brands , which owns Taco Bell and KFC. His comments followed Starbucks’ October 12 denial that it was pursuing an acquisition of Chipotle Mexican Grill , where Niccol previously served as CEO.

The comments came a day after the company reported fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results. Global comparable sales rose 7.2%, while U.S. comparable sales increased 7.7%. Consolidated operating margin expanded 450 basis points YoY to 14%, while EPS grew approximately 54% to $0.80.

Moreover, during the earnings call, Niccol said the results put Starbucks ahead of schedule on its fiscal 2028 framework.

On the market side, shares fell 1.18% to $104.26 on Friday.

data.title: SES and Air Astana Introduce Multi-orbit Inflight Connectivity on A321LR Fleet
data.description:
SES was selected by Air Astana, the award-winning flag carrier of Kazakhstan, to introduce next-generation inflight connectivity services across its Airbus A321LR fleet. The first connected aircraft entered commercial service on 29 October 2026. Fleet-wide deployment will continue across the remaining A321LR fleet.

Equipped with SES’s new electronically steered array (ESA) antenna, the aircraft delivers reliable connectivity over the SES multi-orbit network. SES will provide a fully managed inflight connectivity service across the fleet, enabling Air Astana passengers to enjoy a seamless online experience throughout their journey.

“Airlines are increasingly looking for connectivity solutions that deliver a seamless passenger experience while providing the flexibility to evolve with changing customer expectations,” said Blane Boynton, Senior Vice President, Aviation at SES. “SES's multi-orbit solution will enable Air Astana to offer a consistent, high-quality online experience across its network and bring a new era of inflight connectivity to passengers throughout Central Asia and beyond."

The service supports Air Astana's vision of transforming the onboard experience for both business and leisure travelers. Through an airline-branded connectivity portal, passengers will be able to access a range of connectivity options, including complimentary streaming services for premium customers and flexible paid packages for Economy Class travelers. The service is supported by QMobile, (formerly Jusan Mobile), a leading telecommunications and technology provider in Kazakhstan.

"Today's passengers expect to stay connected wherever they travel, whether they are working, keeping in touch with family and friends, or enjoying entertainment during their journey," said Yelena Obukhova, Vice President, "Our partnership with SES will enable Air Astana to offer a modern, high-quality connectivity experience that reflects the premium service our customers expect. By combining multi-orbit satellite technology with our onboard experience, we are investing in greater comfort, convenience and value for our passengers."

Follow us on:

About SES

At SES, we believe that space has the power to make a difference. That’s why we design space solutions that help governments protect, businesses grow, and people stay connected—no matter where they are. With integrated multi-orbit satellites and our global terrestrial network, we deliver resilient, seamless connectivity and the highest quality video content to those shaping what’s next. Following our Intelsat acquisition, we now offer more than 100 years of combined global industry leadership—backed by a track record of bringing innovation “firsts” to market. As a trusted partner to customers and the global space ecosystem, SES is driving impact that goes far beyond coverage. The company is headquartered in Luxembourg and listed on Paris and Luxembourg stock exchanges (Ticker: SESG). Further information is available at: www.ses.com

About Air Astana

Air Astana is Kazakhstan’s leading full-service airline and the country’s flag carrier. Established in 2002, the airline is part of Air Astana Group. It operates a fleet of Airbus and Boeing aircraft, providing scheduled domestic, regional and international passenger and cargo services across Central Asia, the Caucasus, the Far East, the Gulf, India and Europe. Air Astana has been recognised by Skytrax as the Best Airline in Central Asia & CIS for fourteen consecutive years and has received the Best Airline Staff Service in Central Asia & CIS award nine times in a row. The airline has also been awarded a five-star rating in the Major Airlines category by the Airline Passenger Experience Association.“

data.title: Google AI Spending Shock: Alphabet Loses Over $500 Billion After Q3 Earnings Miss
data.description:
The sell-off followed disappointing advertising revenue, slower Google Search growth, and rising concerns over the cost of its AI expansion. Despite strong Google Cloud performance, investors questioned whether Alphabet's growing infrastructure investments could generate sufficient returns.

Alphabet Q3 Revenue Miss Raises Google Search Concerns

Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.6 billion, representing a 25% increase from $102.3 billion a year earlier. However, the result missed analysts' expectations of approximately $128.2 billion, according to LSEG data.

Sundar Pichai reported Alphabet's Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% year-over-year to $127.6 billion, driven by AI-led growth across its businesses. Source: Sundar Pichai via X

Google advertising revenue reached $82.01 billion, falling about $1.4 billion short of market estimates. Within that segment, Google Search and other advertising revenue increased 12% to $63.35 billion, compared with 17% growth in the previous quarter. YouTube advertising revenue also increased 9% to $11.2 billion.

The slowdown has drawn attention to Google's expanding use of AI-powered search features. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler indicated that increased adoption of AI Mode contributed to the deceleration in search advertising growth. The conversational interface encourages longer interactions, but those queries currently generate less advertising revenue per use than traditional search.

Foreign-exchange movements also affected the quarterly comparison. However, investors remain concerned about how Google's transition toward AI-generated search experiences could affect its established advertising model.

The issue was highlighted by Dave Wagner, portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors. He said, "In a market worried about AI cannibalizing the franchise, investors need to see search accelerating, not decelerating."

His comments reflect a central concern surrounding Alphabet's AI strategy: maintaining search engagement while ensuring that new AI experiences continue to generate advertising revenue.

AI Infrastructure Spending Drives Negative Free Cash Flow

Alphabet's increasing AI investment was another source of investor concern. The company recorded $51.4 billion in capital expenditure during the third quarter, with most of the spending directed toward technical infrastructure supporting AI development and cloud services.

Alphabet reported its first negative free cash flow in 22 years, reaching $9.07 billion as aggressive AI infrastructure investments drove heavy spending on data centers and cloud capacity. Source: Reuters via X

The investment contributed to negative free cash flow of approximately $9.07 billion, compared with a $5.9 billion deficit in the previous quarter. It marked the second consecutive quarter of negative free cash flow and a significant change for a company that had historically generated substantial cash from its operations.

Alphabet's management said the deficit reflected the cost of expanding technical infrastructure, alongside inventory accumulation for Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems and a $5.2 billion cash payment related to a European Commission fine.

The spending also coincided with a decline in reported earnings. Alphabet's net income available to common shareholders fell 25% year over year to $26.17 billion. Diluted earnings per share came in at $2.12, while the company's adjusted EPS was reported at $2.67, below the $3.02 analyst estimate.

An unrealized investment loss also affected the results. Alphabet reported negative $8.2 billion in other income and expenses, primarily because of a decline in the value of its SpaceX investment. The non-cash accounting loss reduced reported earnings but was separate from the company's infrastructure expenditure.

Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi maintained Alphabet's 2026 capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion. However, she told analysts that spending would increase significantly in 2027, without providing a specific figure.

This outlook has raised questions about how quickly the company's AI investments can translate into additional earnings and sustainable cash generation.

Google Cloud Growth and Gemini AI Demand Offer Support

Despite the pressure on advertising, Google Cloud delivered one of Alphabet's strongest quarterly performances. Revenue increased 103% year over year to $30.71 billion, supported by demand for AI infrastructure, enterprise services, and computing capacity.

Alphabet ($GOOGL) fell nearly 13% after missing Q3 2026 revenue and EPS estimates, as slowing search ad growth and investment losses weighed on investor sentiment. Source: @KobeissiLetter via X

Cloud operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion, while its operating margin expanded to 36.2%, compared with 23.7% in the same quarter last year. Alphabet also reported a $561 billion cloud backlog, reflecting substantial contracted demand for its services.

The company's AI products showed further growth. Alphabet's first-party model APIs were processing nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, representing a 40% increase from the previous quarter. The Gemini app also reached one billion users, while the company introduced additional models through its Gemini 4 Argon and Carbon lineup.

CEO Sundar Pichai pointed to increased search engagement as evidence that the company's AI investments were supporting product usage. He said the year-over-year Search query growth rate was "the highest it's been in the last five years."

These developments offer a different perspective from the market's reaction. Google Cloud is benefiting from enterprise demand, while Gemini adoption and AI-powered search are expanding the company's reach.

However, the immediate challenge remains monetization. Alphabet must demonstrate that increased AI usage can generate enough advertising and subscription revenue to justify the substantial costs of building and operating its infrastructure.

GOOG Technical Analysis: $280 Support in Focus

Alphabet's Class C shares (NASDAQ: GOOG) closed at approximately $282.32 on October 29, down 12.29% during the session. The stock also traded near $278.29 at its intraday low, reflecting strong selling pressure following the earnings announcement.

Alphabet Inc (Google) Class C price chart. Source: TradingView

The decline pushed shares below several important short- and medium-term moving averages. TradingView's point to a bearish short-term structure, with downward-sloping averages reinforcing the recent selling pressure. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has also moved toward oversold territory.

However, an oversold RSI reading does not independently confirm a bullish reversal. Traders may look for stabilization and a confirmed recovery above nearby resistance before treating the decline as a potential trend change.

On the downside, the $275-$280 region represents an immediate support area. A sustained break below this zone could expose the stock to additional historical demand levels.

On the upside, the $290 level represents initial resistance, followed by the psychological $300 mark. A broader resistance region extends toward $328.50, where previously broken support levels could influence future price movements.

A sustained recovery above $300 would provide an early indication that selling pressure is easing. Until then, the technical structure remains under pressure, with buyers needing to defend the lower support region.

AI Investment Returns Remain Alphabet's Biggest Test

Alphabet's latest earnings highlight the growing gap between AI demand and the financial cost of meeting it. Google Cloud, Gemini, and AI infrastructure services are attracting customers, but the company is also committing increasingly large sums to data centers, servers, networking equipment, and custom processors.

The pressure could continue into 2027. Management has already indicated that capital expenditure will rise significantly, while greater use of third-party computing capacity could weigh on cloud margins in the near term.

For investors, the central question is whether AI can strengthen Google's existing businesses without weakening the economics of traditional search advertising. Alphabet's expanding cloud business offers an important source of growth, but its search operations remain critical to overall revenue generation.

The latest sell-off shows that investors are increasingly focused on the financial returns from AI rather than spending commitments and product launches alone. Alphabet's ability to convert growing AI adoption into higher revenue, improved margins, and positive free cash flow could become an important factor in determining the stock's next direction.
